name: Muse Gadgets: ESP32 Device SDK
license: Apache-2.0 (third-party exceptions listed in the repo README; the Jollybot avatar is not covered)
summary: Open-source ESP32 firmware that turns an off-the-shelf board into a device for Muse, Meta's personal AI agent. The board pairs to the Muse app over BLE, joins Wi-Fi and holds an encrypted session to your Muse VM.
toolchain: ESP-IDF v6.0.1 only (other versions unsupported); macOS or Linux host.
requires: A Muse account and the Muse app (iOS/Android) with Settings > Devices > Developer mode on
An SDK token (mgst_...) from gadgets.muse.ai > Account > SDK tokens
One of the supported boards below
setup_steps: Get an SDK token at https://gadgets.muse.ai/settings/sdk-tokens (never commit it or paste it into a public repo).

Install ESP-IDF v6.0.1: git clone -b v6.0.1 --recursive https://github.com/espressif/esp-idf.git ~/esp/esp-idf-v6 && ~/esp/esp-idf-v6/install.sh esp32c5,esp32s3,esp32c6,esp32 && . ~/esp/esp-idf-v6/export.sh
Set the token: idf.py menuconfig > ESP32 Device SDK > Muse Gadgets SDK token (or CONFIG_GADGET_SDK_TOKEN in the build's sdkconfig).
Build and flash with the board's command below, then idf.py -p PORT flash monitor. If flashing can't connect: hold BOOT, tap RESET, release BOOT.
In the Muse app: Settings > Devices > Add Device, pick MuseGadget-XXXXXX, press the board's button when the light breathes blue. Green = connected.
agent_quickstart: curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | sh && git clone https://github.com/facebookincubator/muse-gadget-sdk && cd muse-gadget-sdk/esp32 && muse --disable-sandbox   # then: "Build this firmware for my <board> and flash it." Any coding agent that reads AGENTS.md can do the same.

tiers.label: Full UI
tiers.description: LVGL animated avatar, push-to-talk and on-device settings; over-the-air updates on.

tiers.label: Status
tiers.description: Status on a light, LED ring, e-paper or simple screen; over-the-air updates off.

caveats: Boards without PSRAM (classic ESP32, ESP32-C6) run without the home-network tunnel; Muse can still reach and control them.
The home-network tunnel lets Muse reach devices on your LAN that expose a local HTTP API. Treat it like giving the agent a foothold on your network.
Pairing has no manufacturer verification and can't prevent an active man-in-the-middle attack.
Builds are signed with the included development key and never enable Secure Boot. Enable NVS encryption (CONFIG_HOMEHUB_NVS_ENCRYPTION).
Custom ESP32 commands are not a documented API yet: the command set (display.draw_url, sensors.read, camera.capture, ...) is hardcoded in main/app.c.

terms.summary: Personal, non-commercial use with your own Muse account. A token can be linked to at most 50 devices. You may not put it in any device you sell, advertise, or list publicly or in a marketplace or app store; other distribution needs Meta's written permission. Provided as-is; Meta can change, withdraw or revoke access at any time.

boards.note: Status light and button. Muse's recommended starting point.
No PSRAM, so no home-network tunnel; draws images straight to the screen.
Air sensors only on D1S/D1Pro (temp/humidity via the bundled Grove AHT20).
Status text and black-and-white images on 7.5" e-paper.
Status on the LED ring, push-to-talk, dial as volume.
Round AMOLED avatar; best desk object.
No PSRAM: voice notes go over the control session and replies come back as scrolling text.
8 MB flash variant of the Muse partition layout.
End of life at M5Stack; buzzer only, so no spoken replies.

name: Muse Gadgets: Linux Device SDK
summary: A Python service (musegadget) that turns a Linux box with Bluetooth LE into a Muse gadget. Muse gets shell, file and health commands on the machine and can push messages back to you.
toolchain: Python 3.9+, BlueZ, python3-dbus and python3-gi; Raspberry Pi OS Bullseye+, Debian 11+ or Ubuntu 22.04+ (32- or 64-bit); sudo.
requires: A Muse account and the Muse app with Developer mode on
A Linux machine with Bluetooth LE on your network
setup_steps: bash install.sh --sdk-token mgst_...   (installs to /opt/musegadget and starts the musegadget systemd service)
Pair from the Muse app within 10 minutes (device shows as MuseGadgetXXXXXX); re-pair later with sudo musegadget pair.
Optional: push messages to Muse from scripts with musegadget send-user-msg "..."
agent_quickstart: Ask Muse (or any coding agent on the box) things like: "Install Home Assistant on my Pi and tell me how to open it."
extending: Add a spec to COMMAND_SPECS in linux/src/musegadget/executor.py (description, required/optional params with type + description, optional timeout_ms), handle it in Executor.run returning ok(payload) or error(message), then restart the service.

tiers.label: Linux
tiers.description: Shell, file and health commands; scripts can message you through Muse.

caveats: Commands run as the install user with exactly that account's permissions. If it can sudo, so can Muse. Use a dedicated low-privilege user (--run-as USER) unless you need more.
Messages from the device are capped at 256 KB; command output is cut at 96 KB per stream.
Muse labels it a community device; it is not a supported Meta product.

terms.summary: Same token terms as the ESP32 SDK: personal and non-commercial, at most 50 devices per token, no selling or public listing, revocable at any time.

Listed in the Linux SDK README; slow but enough for shell and file commands.
